name: Kepler-538B

boundTo.source: El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021, MNRAS 506, 2269) list Kepler-538 and Kepler-538B in their Gaia EDR3 wide-binary catalogue (VizieR J/MNRAS/506/2269, source_id 2087171453788422528 and 2087171453783512704), 2,679 AU apart on the sky, with a chance-alignment probability of 3.2e-4: the pair is bound. No orbit of the pair is published, and the Gaia astrometry alone does not constrain one, so the star is placed by its own astrometry and carries no orbit.

description: Star bound to Kepler-538, 2,679 AU away.

radius.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the radius of TIC 28227107 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

mass.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the mass of TIC 28227107 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

temperature.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the effective temperature of TIC 28227107 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

text.card: Kepler-538B is a star of 3,386 K, bound to Kepler-538 2,679 AU away.
text.introduction: Kepler-538B shares its motion through space with Kepler-538, 2,679 AU away, so the two are a bound pair. Both are placed where Gaia measures them.

notes: Kepler-538B's orbit around Kepler-538 is not measured; both stars are placed at their Gaia DR3 positions, which is where they are

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 2087171453783512704 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 50,000 of its distance per century
